results.primary_cause: Current dry-bulk freight conditions are supported by higher Capesize demand and tightening vessel supply, although the strength may be partly temporary and vulnerable to future fleet oversupply.

supporting_evidence.claim: A key dry-bulk freight measure reached its highest level since December 2023 in May 2026, driven by rising Capesize demand and tightening ship supply.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Dry-Bulk Shipping Rates Hit Two-Year High on Capesize Demand

supporting_evidence.claim: BIMCO warned that apparent 2026 dry-bulk strength was substantially affected by forced rerouting and could reverse as conditions normalize.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Dry bulk shipping faces 2027 supply glut: BIMCO warns Hormuz rerouting boost will reverse

counter_evidence.claim: The reported 2026 dry-bulk strength may be substantially artificial because of forced rerouting, with a potential 2027 supply glut reversing the improvement.
